c6254d487ee7.title: Operations Strategy Analyst
c6254d487ee7.description:
Handle Recruitment is looking for a highly organised and driven Operations Strategy Analyst to provide analytical and project support to the Operations Strategy team at our client's growing sports business.
 £35,000 to £40,000 based on experience 
 London Based | Hybrid - 3 Days In Office 
 The Client 
Our client is not your typical sports organisation. They are a global sports business, co-owned by professional athletes, with a mission to celebrate and elevate triathlon like never before.
2026 marks an exciting new chapter. Following the acquisition of Challenge Family and a strategic partnership with World Triathlon, they are expanding their global reach and creating a more connected future for the sport.
Looking ahead to 2027, the organisation is focused on delivering an even bigger global event portfolio, elevating the athlete and fan experience, and establishing triathlon as a truly global sports and entertainment property.
 This is a rare opportunity to join a high-performing, high-energy and values-driven team, with leadership talent from UFC, RFU, Uber, Meta, ATP and Formula 1, all passionate about building something extraordinary.
 The Role 
You'll dive deep into data, identify bottlenecks and help turn high-level strategy into actionable, day-to-day improvements. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys getting hands-on with data to understand the "why" behind the "what".
You'll contribute to ambitious, industry-defining projects, learn through experimentation and help shape the future of triathlon within a fast-paced, growing organisation.
Reporting to the Business Strategy Associate, the role is based at our client's London HQ.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Strategic Support 
 Lead specific strategic projects, such as developing pricing strategies for new events, from data gathering through to the final product.
 Turn one-off operational tasks into standardised, repeatable processes and documentation.
 Maintain performance dashboards covering revenue, cost optimisation and efficiency metrics.
 Analyse operational data to identify trends, opportunities and red flags.
 Support high-quality presentations and reports for senior and executive audiences, translating data into clear charts and visualisations.
 Conduct benchmarking and market research against competitors, industry standards and best practices.
 Project Coordination 
 Act as the "drumbeat" for strategic initiatives, keeping project trackers updated and deadlines on track.
 Support the Business Strategy Associate in coordinating with departments to gather requirements and maintain project alignment.
 Map current-state versus ideal-state processes to identify opportunities for improvement.
 About You 
 1-2 years' experience in an analytical role such as Operations, Consulting or Strategy, ideally within sports or events.
 Excellent attention to detail and strong analytical skills.
 Advanced Excel / Google Sheets skills, including Lookups, Pivot Tables and basic modelling.
 Familiarity with Google Slides and presenting data clearly.
 The ability to turn complex tasks into simple, actionable updates.
 Natural curiosity and a willingness to ask "why" and "how".
 A proactive, get-things-done mentality, with a focus on identifying solutions, not just problems.
 The ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment where priorities can shift.
 A collaborative approach and desire to support shared goals.
 An awareness of industry trends and emerging technologies.
 What Our Client Offers 
 The opportunity to make a genuine impact within triathlon and contribute to an ambitious, growing organisation.
 A flat, collaborative and get-things-done working environment.
 Private health insurance through Vitality, including wellness benefits.
 Learning & Development budget for courses, books, events and more.
 25 days' holiday plus a Christmas break.
 Flexible working structure.
 Enhanced parental leave.
 Company share option scheme, giving employees the opportunity to share in the company's success.
 Complimentary / discounted event entries for employees, friends and family.
 Free office snacks and drinks, open water swim credits and more.
 Apply below today if you feel you have the relevant skillset! 
 Handle actively welcomes applicants from under-represented backgrounds - we pride ourselves on attracting the best talent for every opportunity through a commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion.

Associate Consultant – Financial Services (Associate Consulting Programme) 
 Location: London (Hybrid) | Practice Area : Business Consulting | Type: Permanent
 Start your consulting career helping financial services organisations transform how they operate and innovate. 
 The Role 
Capco’s Associate Consulting Programme (ACP) is designed for early-career professionals looking to begin a consulting career within Financial Services. As an Associate Consultant, you will join a cohort of new consultants and complete a structured training programme before working on real client projects.
 You will be aligned to a core domain: Banking & Payments, Capital Markets, Insurance, or Wealth & Asset Management, gaining exposure to transformation initiatives and AI-enabled ways of working. Working alongside experienced consultants, you will help clients modernise platforms, improve operations, and respond to an evolving industry landscape.
 What You’ll Do 
 Support transformation initiatives across Financial Services, conducting research, data analysis, and process mapping to solve client problems
 Develop key project artefacts including requirements, presentations, and analysis outputs while contributing to business analysis, testing, and operational change
 Participate in client meetings and workshops, collaborating with stakeholders and using tools, accelerators, and AI to deliver data-driven outcomes
 What We’re Looking For 
 University graduate with a minimum of a 2.1 grade (or equivalent) at undergraduate level, possessing strong communication, presentation, analytical, and problem-solving skills & able to structure complex information clearly
 Interest in Consulting and Financial Services, with curiosity & knowledge of trends across one or more or our domains
 Experience using AI tools and a strong interest in how AI is shaping the future of work
 Proactive, curious, and collaborative mindset with strong attention to detail
 Bonus Points For 
 6 months’ experience in consulting, financial services, fintech, or technology, with exposure to transformation, operations, or regulatory concepts
 Familiarity with data analysis tools, AI, or emerging technologies, and experience working in team-based or project environments
 Demonstrated interest in innovation, Financial Services trends, or technology accelerators such as AI-enabled tooling
 Why Join Capco 
 Start your consulting career with structured training and hands-on project experience
 Work on transformation initiatives across leading Financial Services organisations
 Learn from experienced consultants in a collaborative, entrepreneurial culture
 Be part of a team shaping the future of Financial Services
 Help build the next generation of consulting talent at Capco
 Associate Consulting Programme Structure 
You’ll begin with a two-week immersive training programme covering Financial Services fundamentals, consulting skills, and real-world case simulations.
 Following this, you’ll join a client project, supported by a dedicated career coach and peer buddy, whilst continuing to receive ongoing learning through training, certifications, and on-the-job experience.
 We offer a competitive, people-first benefits package designed to support every aspect of your life:
 Core Benefits : Discretionary bonus, competitive pension, health insurance, life insurance and critical illness cover

We’re committed to making our recruitment process accessible and straightforward for everyone. If you need any adjustments at any stage, just let us know – we’ll be happy to help. Next Generation Fellowship Programme (PhD) 
 Location: London (Hybrid) | Practice Area: Technology & Engineering | Type: Permanent
 Start Date: 1st February 2027 - you must be available to join on this date in order to participate in the induction and follow-on training provided. 
 Fast-track your career in technology consulting through one of Capco's flagship early careers programmes. 
 The Role 
 Our Next Generation Fellowship Programme is designed for exceptional recent or upcoming doctoral graduates who want to apply their research expertise to solving complex business and technology challenges.
 Running for over ten years, the programme accelerates technically gifted individuals into consulting careers, providing opportunities to work alongside experienced consultants, former fellows, and industry experts on some of the most innovative transformation programmes in financial services.
 As a Fellow, you will bridge the gap between business strategy and technology implementation, helping clients solve complex challenges through research, analysis, innovation, and technology. You’ll also explore how approved AI tools, automation, and AI-enabled ways of working can improve the speed, quality, and insight of your work, while applying human judgement and responsible AI practices.
 The variety of work means no two projects are the same, allowing you to develop expertise across multiple domains while shaping your own career path.
 What You’ll Do 
 Contribute to technology strategy, digital transformation, cloud adoption and modernisation programmes for financial services clients.

 Support projects involving artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, resilience, sustainability and large-scale transformation.

 Help design and test new fintech ventures, innovation pilots and proofs of concept, collaborating with technical and business stakeholders throughout delivery.
 What We’re Looking For 
 A doctorate (PhD, EngD, or equivalent), in a STEM discipline, alongside a minimum 2:1 undergraduate degree or international equivalent.
 Exceptional analytical and problem-solving abilities, with the ability to communicate complex ideas clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
 Strong collaboration skills, with the confidence to demonstrate leadership when appropriate and work effectively across different stakeholder groups.
 Adaptability, intellectual curiosity and a genuine passion for learning, innovation and solving complex problems.
 Curiosity about using approved AI tools and automation to improve productivity and insight, combined with sound human judgement and an understanding of the importance of responsible use, review and escalation where needed.
 Bonus Points For 
 Knowledge of technologies used within financial services, including cloud computing, AI (including Generative AI and Agentic AI), machine learning, blockchain or modern software engineering.
 Awareness of financial services trends such as digital banking, fintech innovation, payments, sustainability, digital assets or emerging lending models.
 Programming or software development experience, particularly in prototyping, modelling, machine learning, data analysis or proof-of-concept development.
 Experience collaborating with technical and business stakeholders in research, commercial or practical environments.

Elixirr International plc is a global consulting firm with a bold ambition: to become the best consulting firm in the world.

 **Experience working in the insurance sector is ESSENTIAL** 
 Your new company 
A growing insurance business is seeking an Assistant Management Accountant to join its London finance team. The organisation operates within the specialist insurance market and provides solutions across a diverse range of commercial risks. Following continued growth, the business is strengthening its finance function to support increasing reporting requirements, maintain robust financial controls and provide high-quality management information. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing organisation and gain broad exposure across insurance accounting, financial reporting, data analysis and business partnering and get the opportunity to work with some of the best names in the industry!
 Your new role 
As Assistant Management Accountant, you will work closely with the Finance Manager and wider business to deliver accurate and timely financial information. The role will have a strong focus on management reporting, insurance data validation and business partnering with underwriting, claims and other operational stakeholders. You will gain exposure to a broad range of finance activities, making this an excellent opportunity for a part-qualified accountant who is looking to develop their technical insurance accounting experience within a growing business.
 Key responsibilities will include: 
 Preparing management information covering premiums, commissions, claims and other key financial performance measures.
 Extracting and analysing information from underwriting, claims and reserving systems.
 Reviewing insurance data to ensure information is complete, accurate and consistent with the relevant contracts and supporting documentation.
 Analysing paid and outstanding claims information and investigating potential anomalies within financial and operational data.
 Partnering with underwriting, claims and operational teams to respond to queries and provide meaningful financial insight.
 Preparing and posting non-technical expense journals, ensuring entries are accurate and supported by appropriate documentation.
 Supporting the month-end close process, including general ledger and trial balance activities.
 Assisting with the preparation of monthly profit and loss accounts and balance sheets across multiple business areas.
 Producing performance analysis to support commercial, underwriting and claims-related decision-making.
 Developing and maintaining financial dashboards and key performance indicators for internal stakeholders.
 Supporting the preparation of statutory accounts, regulatory reporting and tax-related submissions.
 Assisting with premium, claims and commission reporting for external insurance partners.
 Contributing to financial process improvements, automation initiatives and wider financial transformation projects.
 Supporting ad hoc reporting, analysis and project work as required.
 What you'll need to succeed 
 Part-qualified status through ACCA, CIMA or ACA, with a commitment to completing your professional qualification and actively studying towards completion. 
 ****Previous accounting experience gained within the insurance sector**** 
 A good understanding of insurance accounting principles and financial reporting requirements.t.
 An understanding of insurance and reinsurance arrangements and how premiums, commissions and claims are recorded.
 Experience preparing management accounts, management information or financial performance reporting.
 Strong analytical skills and the ability to identify inconsistencies or anomalies within large volumes of data.
 Strong attention to detail and the ability to work accurately within reporting deadlines.
 What you'll get in return 
 Permanent opportunity within the specialist insurance market.
 Hybrid working arrangement.
 Exposure to management accounting, insurance reporting and commercial finance.
 The opportunity to work closely with underwriting, claims and operational stakeholders.
 Broad exposure across multiple areas of the finance function.
 Supportive environment for a part-qualified accountant looking to continue their professional development.
 The chance to contribute to process automation and finance transformation initiatives.
 Excellent long-term development opportunities within a growing business.

 CRA’s Life Sciences Practice helps pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical devices and digital health companies achieve optimum performance across key aspects of their business including commercial strategy, pricing and access, innovation, organisation structure, policy analysis, medical affairs, stakeholder management, and reputation, all for the long-term benefit of patients, clinicians, employees, and shareholders. We work with life sciences businesses directly as well as with their legal counsel, industry associations, government organisations, and advocacy groups.
 The CRA Life Sciences team operates from offices across the United States, UK and Europe, providing insights on global issues and local market challenges across all geographies.    
 Our clients’ trust in us is rooted in our emphatic focus on clients and specifically our hands-on life sciences experience, in-depth sector knowledge, from R&D to market entry and beyond, and strong academic credentials in science, economics, policy and business.     
 Our dedicated Policy team works with Life Sciences companies, industry associations, government organizations, and advocacy groups to anticipate and respond to policy challenges. Our projects focus on analysing ongoing or anticipated policy challenges, assessing the impact on patients, competition or innovation, and helping clients with developing solutions that address these challenges whilst supporting their commercial priorities.     
 During your internship you may work on a variety of project types, including but not limited to:     
 Policy projects: helps clients anticipate how healthcare policies will evolve and what this means for access to medicines and future innovation. Projects range from US debates on drug pricing and Medicare negotiations to global challenges around cell and gene therapies, healthcare financing, and digital health   
 Opportunity assessment : Supporting the valuation of new therapies     
 Value communication : Building evidence-based narratives to demonstrate the clinical and economic value of new medicines     
 Market access planning & payer strategy : Mapping regulatory pathways, evidence needs, reimbursement hurdles and innovative solutions across geographies     
 Forecasting & pricing strategy : Developing models to project product performance, define the optimal launch and lifecycle price of a therapy, inform launch planning activities     
 Commercial strategy & lifecycle planning : Designing go-to-market models and strategies to sustain brand value and portfolio planning

You will join project teams working on high-impact challenges in life sciences, with opportunities to learn, contribute, and grow.

 Work closely with senior colleagues on strategy and policy projects that address real client needs    
 Conduct research and analyse both qualitative insights and quantitative data    
 Contribute your ideas to team discussions and see how your analysis feeds into client deliverables    
 Attend client meetings and expert interviews, gaining exposure to real-world stakeholder perspectives    
 Draft sections of reports, presentations, and Excel models, supported by senior team members    
 Develop your knowledge of the life sciences industry and consulting methodologies    
 Take part in training and practice-building activities    
 Alongside this project work, you will have a Professional Development Manager dedicated to your growth, an onboarding buddy for day-to-day support, and regular feedback from project managers    
 Desired Qualifications     
 Penultimate year or final year Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD degree candidates with strong academic performance from a top-tier institution (minimum 2:1) with focused study in biological sciences, economics (or related subjects including business, health economics and policy, public policy), physical sciences, mathematics, statistics, engineering, or other STEM discipline;    
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Outlook and Excel), plus an understanding of how to conduct internet research    
 Proficiency using and analysing quantitative data to answer questions;    
 Experience with, or keen interest in, Life Sciences industry and healthcare;    
 Understanding of economic concepts and business processes, as well as familiarity with essential consulting methodologies, tools and techniques;    
 Effective written and oral communication and presentation skills (additional languages beyond English are helpful);    
 Strong self-management (detail orientation, effective time management, ability to prioritise);    
 Demonstrated high level of initiative and leadership;    
 Excellent teamwork and collaboration capabilities;    
 Clear and demonstrated interest in consulting through coursework, work experience, activities, or attendance at CRA recruiting events;    
 Willingness and ability to undertake occasional travel to clients if required.   
 To Apply     
 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis starting from 2 October 2026 . We will begin inviting candidates for video interviews from 16 November 2026 onwards. We strongly encourage early applications, as interview slots will be offered on a first-come, first-served basis, and will close applications once the positions are filled.     
 To be considered for this position, please submit the following:    
 Resume/CV: please include current address, personal email and telephone number;    
 Cover letter:   please describe your interest in CRA and how this role matches your goals. Your cover letter should be no more than one page, and presented in a clear, professional manner (minimum font size 12).  Please ensure your cover letter answers the following questions:    
 Why life sciences consulting, and why CRA?    
 What is an example of a time when you made a data-guided decision?    
 Which experience from your resume/CV are you most proud of and why?    
 The internship will take place from Monday 28 th June 2027 – Friday 3 rd September 2027.   
 Professional Development      
 CRA’s robust skills development programs and wellness programming encourage you to thrive as an individual and team member. We provide interns a variety of technical training, presentation skills, internal seminars, and performance coaching over the summer.    
 Work Location Flexibility 
 CRA creates a work environment that enables our colleagues to benefit from being together in the office to best deliver on our promise of career growth, mentorship and inclusivity. At the same time, we recognise that individuals realise a range of benefits when working from home periodically. We currently ask that individuals spend 3 to 4 days a week on average working in the office (which may include traveling to another CRA office or to a client's location), with specific days determined in coordination with your practice or team.
 Our Commitment to Diversity
